newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: One dead, 10 hurt in Bangladesh political clash.
newsitem.headline: One dead, 10 hurt in Bangladesh political clash.

text.p: One man was shot dead and 10 injured in clashes between government and opposition supporters in Bangladesh's southeastern town of Feni on Saturday, police said.
Police identified the dead man as Mohammad Nasir, an activist of the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) which is headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
The town of Feni is Khaleda's ancestral home.
Police said they could not identify who fired the shots.

They said violence started as BNP supporters took to the street to protest the earlier killing of a party student leader, Ashrafur Rahman Tushar. BNP and Awami activists battled with guns, stones, iron rods and sticks, they added.
Tushar, 25, was fatally injured in Feni on Thursday night after an attack, apparently by activists of the ruling Awami League. He died in hospital early on Friday.
Angry BNP protesters later burned five vehicles and damaged several others, police and witnesses said.
The BNP had called for a half-day general strike at Feni on Saturday over Tushar's killing.
Local authorities called in paramilitary troops, and police said the situation was under control but remained very tense.
